title: The Catcher in the Rye
synopsis: Pencey Prep, December. You've been expelled. You take the train to New York. You have three days before your parents find out.

nodes.text: Stradlater is, you think, a phony. You leave with a hat.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Brave.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Wise.

nodes.text: Mothers across the aisle. You lie about her son.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Lie kindly” back. Care shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honest.

nodes.text: Cab. Phoenix wanted, hotel suggested.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Path—follows you into whatever comes next.
There is no taking “Walk” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Three women from Seattle. Dancing.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Lonely.
You commit to “Leave.” The story records the instinct as “Wise” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: An elevator boy sends up a girl. You decide not to.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honest.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Lonely—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Maurice takes more money. Your nose bleeds.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honest.
“Plan revenge” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Foolish.

nodes.text: You take her ice skating. You ask her to run away.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Stop yourself” back. Wise shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Foolish.

nodes.text: Old schoolmate. He is, charitably, a snob.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Civil.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honest.

nodes.text: Late night, you call Sally. You apologize, sort of.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Get home.” The story records the instinct as “Wise” and carries it forward.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honest.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Wonder.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You sneak home. Your sister is, against everything, a real person.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Tell her you're going west” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: The mummies. The display cases. You always loved that things stayed the same.

choices.consequence: “Sit” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest.
“Walk” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Survive.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Tell her no” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Central Park. She rides. It rains.

nodes.text: Your brother visits. He drives a fancy car. He is, in his way, kind.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Forgive him.” The story records the instinct as “Brother” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You're going to a new school in the fall.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Try” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You realize you miss everyone. Even Stradlater.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honest.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Pride.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You go to the new school. You do, eventually, finish. You also, slowly, stop hating most people. You realize the phonies were, often, just scared like you.
You become a writer in your twenties. You write a long careful book about a few days in December when you almost ran away. The book becomes a kind of mirror for decades of teenagers.
You stay close to Phoebe for the rest of your life. She becomes a teacher. You become her brother in the way that matters. You are, in middle age, happy.
